group.description: Models Eclipse core-expressions property testers from plugin.xml, resolves them to the Java type graph, and validates that declarations are wired up (existing implementation class, resolvable receiver type) and that view-model types are covered by a tester.

concept.description: Labels <propertyTester> elements declared under an <extension point="org.eclipse.core.expressions.propertyTesters"> as :Eclipse:PropertyTester and creates DECLARES_PROPERTY_TESTER relationships from the bundle. Extracts id, type (receiver type), namespace, properties, and class attributes onto the node.
concept.cypher: MATCH (bundle:Osgi:Bundle)-[:DECLARES_EXTENSION]->(ext:Eclipse:Extension) WHERE ext.point = 'org.eclipse.core.expressions.propertyTesters' MATCH (ext)-[:HAS_ELEMENT]->(pt:Xml:Element {name: 'propertyTester'}) OPTIONAL MATCH (pt)-[:HAS_ATTRIBUTE]->(idAttr:Xml:Attribute {name: 'id'}) OPTIONAL MATCH (pt)-[:HAS_ATTRIBUTE]->(typeAttr:Xml:Attribute {name: 'type'}) OPTIONAL MATCH (pt)-[:HAS_ATTRIBUTE]->(nsAttr:Xml:Attribute {name: 'namespace'}) OPTIONAL MATCH (pt)-[:HAS_ATTRIBUTE]->(propsAttr:Xml:Attribute {name: 'properties'}) OPTIONAL MATCH (pt)-[:HAS_ATTRIBUTE]->(classAttr:Xml:Attribute {name: 'class'}) SET pt:Eclipse:PropertyTester, pt.propertyTesterId = idAttr.value, pt.testerType = typeAttr.value, pt.namespace = nsAttr.value, pt.properties = propsAttr.value, pt.testerClass = classAttr.value MERGE (bundle)-[:DECLARES_PROPERTY_TESTER]->(pt) RETURN bundle.bundleSymbolicName AS Bundle, pt.testerType AS ReceiverType, pt.namespace AS Namespace, pt.properties AS Properties, pt.testerClass AS TesterClass ORDER BY Bundle, ReceiverType

concept.description: For each :Eclipse:PropertyTester with a `type` attribute, creates a TESTS_TYPE relationship to the matching :Type resolved within the declaring bundle's class space -- the host bundle plus the host's attached fragments, since a fragment shares the host's classloader. When the same fully qualified type is provided by both the host and a fragment, the host copy is preferred, mirroring OSGi host-first class loading. Types in unrelated bundles are intentionally NOT matched.
concept.cypher: MATCH (declaring:Osgi:Bundle)-[:DECLARES_PROPERTY_TESTER]->(pt:Eclipse:PropertyTester) WHERE pt.testerType IS NOT NULL AND pt.testerType =~ '^[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$.]*$' // host = the declaring bundle itself, or its host if the declaring bundle is a fragment OPTIONAL MATCH (declaring)-[:FRAGMENT_OF]->(h:Osgi:Bundle) WITH pt, coalesce(h, declaring) AS host // resolve the receiver type within the host's class space (host + its fragments) MATCH (member:Osgi:Bundle)-[:CONTAINS]->(type:Type {fqn: pt.testerType}) WHERE member = host OR (member)-[:FRAGMENT_OF]->(host) WITH pt, collect({t: type, inHost: member = host}) AS cands // prefer the host copy; otherwise take a fragment copy WITH pt, coalesce([c IN cands WHERE c.inHost][0].t, cands[0].t) AS chosen WHERE chosen IS NOT NULL MERGE (pt)-[:TESTS_TYPE]->(chosen) RETURN DISTINCT pt.testerType AS ReceiverType, chosen.fqn AS ResolvedType ORDER BY ReceiverType

concept.description: For each :Eclipse:PropertyTester with a `class` attribute, creates an IMPLEMENTED_BY relationship to the implementing :Type (the class that extends org.eclipse.core.expressions.PropertyTester) resolved within the declaring bundle's class space -- the host bundle plus its attached fragments. When the class is provided by both the host and a fragment, the host copy is preferred. Types in unrelated bundles are intentionally NOT matched.
concept.cypher: MATCH (declaring:Osgi:Bundle)-[:DECLARES_PROPERTY_TESTER]->(pt:Eclipse:PropertyTester) WHERE pt.testerClass IS NOT NULL AND pt.testerClass =~ '^[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$.]*$' OPTIONAL MATCH (declaring)-[:FRAGMENT_OF]->(h:Osgi:Bundle) WITH pt, coalesce(h, declaring) AS host MATCH (member:Osgi:Bundle)-[:CONTAINS]->(type:Type {fqn: pt.testerClass}) WHERE member = host OR (member)-[:FRAGMENT_OF]->(host) WITH pt, collect({t: type, inHost: member = host}) AS cands WITH pt, coalesce([c IN cands WHERE c.inHost][0].t, cands[0].t) AS chosen WHERE chosen IS NOT NULL MERGE (pt)-[:IMPLEMENTED_BY]->(chosen) RETURN DISTINCT pt.testerClass AS TesterClass, chosen.fqn AS ResolvedType ORDER BY TesterClass

concept.description: Labels :Type nodes whose fully qualified name matches the `viewModelPattern` regular expression as :Eclipse:ViewModelType. These are the types expected to be covered by a property tester. The default pattern matches type names ending in "ViewModel"; override it to fit the project's naming or package convention.
concept.cypher: MATCH (type:Type) WHERE type.fqn =~ $viewModelPattern SET type:Eclipse:ViewModelType RETURN type.fqn AS ViewModelType, coalesce(type.abstract, false) AS IsAbstract ORDER BY ViewModelType

constraint.description: A property tester declares a `class` that does not resolve to any :Type in the graph. The implementation class is shipped by the declaring bundle, so a missing class means the declaration is broken and the tester will fail to load at runtime.
constraint.cypher: MATCH (bundle:Osgi:Bundle)-[:DECLARES_PROPERTY_TESTER]->(pt:Eclipse:PropertyTester) WHERE pt.testerClass IS NOT NULL AND NOT (pt)-[:IMPLEMENTED_BY]->(:Type) AND bundle:Osgi:Analyzed RETURN bundle.bundleSymbolicName AS Bundle, pt.testerClass AS MissingTesterClass, pt.testerType AS ReceiverType, pt.namespace AS Namespace ORDER BY Bundle, MissingTesterClass

constraint.description: A property tester declares a receiver `type` that does not resolve to any :Type in the graph. This is only a genuine defect when the receiver type's bundle is part of the scan; otherwise it merely indicates an out-of-scope type.
constraint.cypher: MATCH (bundle:Osgi:Bundle)-[:DECLARES_PROPERTY_TESTER]->(pt:Eclipse:PropertyTester) WHERE pt.testerType IS NOT NULL AND NOT (pt)-[:TESTS_TYPE]->(:Type) AND bundle:Osgi:Analyzed RETURN bundle.bundleSymbolicName AS Bundle, pt.testerType AS UnresolvedReceiverType, pt.testerClass AS TesterClass ORDER BY Bundle, UnresolvedReceiverType

concept.description: Labels <test> elements (as used in enablement, visibleWhen, activeWhen and reusable expression definitions) that carry a `property` attribute as :Eclipse:PropertyReference, and stores the referenced fully qualified property (namespace + "." + name) in the property attribute. This is the consumer side of property testers.
concept.cypher: MATCH (bundle:Osgi:Bundle)-[:DECLARES_EXTENSION]->(ext:Eclipse:Extension) -[:HAS_ELEMENT*1..12]->(test:Xml:Element {name: 'test'}) -[:HAS_ATTRIBUTE]->(propAttr:Xml:Attribute {name: 'property'}) WHERE propAttr.value IS NOT NULL AND propAttr.value CONTAINS '.' SET test:Eclipse:PropertyReference, test.property = propAttr.value RETURN DISTINCT test.property AS Property ORDER BY Property

concept.description: Creates SATISFIED_BY relationships from an :Eclipse:PropertyReference to any :Eclipse:PropertyTester that declares the referenced property, i.e. a tester whose namespace and one of its comma-separated properties concatenate to the reference's fully qualified property. Property testers are matched globally (the expression framework resolves properties across all contributors).
concept.cypher: MATCH (ref:Eclipse:PropertyReference) MATCH (pt:Eclipse:PropertyTester) WHERE pt.namespace IS NOT NULL AND pt.properties IS NOT NULL AND any(p IN split(pt.properties, ',') WHERE trim(p) <> '' AND pt.namespace + '.' + trim(p) = ref.property) MERGE (ref)-[:SATISFIED_BY]->(pt) RETURN DISTINCT ref.property AS Property, pt.namespace AS Namespace ORDER BY Property

constraint.description: Finds <test property="..."> references whose namespace is owned by a declared property tester but whose property is not provided by any tester in that namespace. This typically indicates a typo in the property name or a property that was removed from the tester, silently breaking the enablement expression.
constraint.cypher: MATCH (bundle:Osgi:Bundle)-[:DECLARES_EXTENSION]->(ext:Eclipse:Extension) -[:HAS_ELEMENT*1..12]->(ref:Eclipse:PropertyReference) WHERE NOT (ref)-[:SATISFIED_BY]->(:Eclipse:PropertyTester) AND bundle:Osgi:Analyzed AND EXISTS { MATCH (pt:Eclipse:PropertyTester) WHERE pt.namespace IS NOT NULL AND ref.property STARTS WITH pt.namespace + '.' } RETURN DISTINCT bundle.bundleSymbolicName AS Bundle, ext.point AS Point, ref.property AS UnsatisfiedProperty ORDER BY Bundle, UnsatisfiedProperty

constraint.description: A property tester declared in a host bundle's plugin.xml has an implementation `class` that is provided only by one of the host's fragments, not by the host itself. The declaration is resolvable only when that fragment is attached, creating an implicit host-to-fragment dependency that reverses the normal fragment-to-host direction.
constraint.cypher: MATCH (host:Osgi:Bundle)-[:DECLARES_PROPERTY_TESTER]->(pt:Eclipse:PropertyTester) WHERE NOT (host)-[:FRAGMENT_OF]->(:Osgi:Bundle) AND pt.testerClass IS NOT NULL AND host:Osgi:Analyzed AND NOT (host)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Type {fqn: pt.testerClass}) MATCH (host)<-[:FRAGMENT_OF]-(frag:Osgi:Bundle)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Type {fqn: pt.testerClass}) RETURN host.bundleSymbolicName AS Host, pt.testerClass AS TesterClass, pt.testerType AS ReceiverType, collect(DISTINCT frag.bundleSymbolicName) AS ResolvedOnlyViaFragments ORDER BY Host, TesterClass

constraint.description: A concrete :Eclipse:ViewModelType has no property tester registered for it or any of its supertypes/interfaces. Such a type cannot be used with custom property-based enablement expressions. This is a project-convention check driven by the `viewModelPattern` parameter of eclipse:ViewModelType.
